read_locations.finding: DivisionRing requires nontrivial ring and inverse law for nonzero inputs; it also imposes totalized inv_zero=0. Field extends CommRing and DivisionRing.
read_locations.obligation: IR3 must construct each nonzero cut inverse and prove the identity before DQ4 names a field. Book Inv has domain R^× and does not adopt totalized zero inversion or division. Source inv_zero is a convention, not 0·0=1.

read_locations.finding: GroupWithZero includes a total inverse with inv_zero=0, and mul_inv_cancel only under a≠0. Multiplication/division cancellation lemmas explicitly preserve nonzero hypotheses.
read_locations.obligation: Use as a definition/condition comparison only. IR3 and DQ1/2 write all domain/nonzero checks and prove identities with cut associativity. Do not import a GroupWithZero instance before providing inverse witnesses.

read_locations.finding: Ordered-field obligations: ordered addition, positive products and 0<1; old combined structures are deprecated in this tag in favor of separate Field/LinearOrder/IsStrictOrderedRing assumptions.
read_locations.obligation: DQ4 lists proved cut field and order obligations. Do not infer any missing inverse existence from an order structure. No Lean instance or compilation claimed.

read_locations.finding: Existing ordered semifield assumptions precede positive reciprocal order statements and midpoint inequalities.
read_locations.obligation: IR1/2 use only Q, whose corresponding arithmetic has already been proved. DQ3 reciprocal order for cuts comes later from constructed inverses and SR3, not from these field-assuming source lemmas.

read_locations.finding: Least-upper-bound property requires every nonempty upper-bounded subset to have a least upper bound; called Dedekind completeness.
read_locations.obligation: DQ4 explicitly uses this meaning only and preserves both nonempty and bounded hypotheses; no Cauchy completeness or uniqueness theorem is thereby supplied.

read_locations.finding: Field axiom list includes 1≠0, nonzero inverse existence, and distributivity; ordered field adds ordered translation and positive product.
read_locations.obligation: Source begins axiomatically; book must prove IR2/3 rather than assume source M5. Use as precise structure checklist after cut construction.

read_locations.finding: Historical §VI says quotients and other elementary operations can be defined, without giving this strict one-sided positive outer-point reciprocal and complete ε witness proof.
read_locations.obligation: History only. I(A), ε=a0(1−q) and q=0 case are independent book derivations, not claimed quotations or externally supplied full proofs.

current_batch25_obligations.obligation: Only A>0: I(A) consists of rational q below1/r for a positive rational exterior r. Positive exterior witnesses place all q≤0 inside; a positive interior a0 gives exterior1/a0 using a0<r. Prove downward closure and no greatest member with rational midpoints, then positivity and positive-domain function closure.

Prove both member inclusions P(A,I(A))=i(1). Reverse q<0 uses P negative branch; for0≤q<1 choose ε=a0(1−q)>0 and DA1 u∈A,v∉A with gap<ε. Interior/exterior separation gives v>a0>0, not u≥a0. Strict chain gives u>qv≥0, includingq=0; rational b betweenq/u and1/v supplies legal positive product witnesses. No cut inverse, real Archimedean theorem, limit or supremum is assumed.

Inv defined only on nonzero cuts. Negative branch N(I(N(A))) has legal positive I input and is negative; positive branch positive. Prove both inverse products, then uniqueness from associativity and an already constructed inverse. Zero has no inverse because0≠1; do not import a totalized inv_zero convention.

Use rational inverse identity and SP4 before uniqueness to obtain Inv(i(r))=i(1/r), onlyr≠0. Check each domain for inverse of1, inverse of inverse and inverse of negation. Examples do not replace all-cut proof.

Define quotient onlyR×R_nonzero→R as A⊗Inv(B). Derive both multiplication-back identities explicitly from inverse/associativity, handle zero numerator, prohibit zero denominator, and prove rational compatibility fors≠0.

Declare solution sets with candidate domainR and R-valued sides. ForC⊗X=D, prove existence and necessity whenC≠0 and both coefficient-zero branches(allR or empty). Show actual two-sided inverse of fixed nonzero multiplication map, then affine equation reduction and its three parameter branches.

Only nonzero denominators: Inv(C) has the same sign, so apply priorSR3 to explicit quotient definitions, with full weak/strict two-way positive and negative chains. For positiveA,B, a positive common inverse product yields reciprocal reversal; do not claim uniform reversal acrosszero. Division byzero remains undefined.

AfterIR3 exists, match all nontrivial commutative-ring and inverse obligations before naming a field; retain same cut set and inclusion order for ordered-field laws. Completeness means exactly existingDC4 nonempty bounded-above subset supremum as union, with conditions and rational member formula explicit. No Cauchy equivalence, uniqueness isomorphism, root existence, real Archimedean theorem or limits is implied.
